review.summary:
The sink, replayer and tests exist, and the acceptance command passes (verify.json). Three things are asserted without being shown: that the replay "cross-checks" the proof files, that 199 traces are clean, and that the heartbeat guard "can fail". summary.md is empty, so there are no agent claims there.
Not met: the replayer re-encodes the guards as copies and does not drive the machine of core_invariants.py/commit_point.py as the brief says. The step-name test only checks literal names, not the replayer's steps.
The endpoint-expiry heartbeat check in replay.py is circular: the sink emits heartbeat_lost immediately before it, so the check cannot fail.
The "broken governor" fixtures check only the event kind in the message, not the step or reason, so they would pass on an unrelated refusal.
Question: should a replay exempt a test by name (FAULT_INJECTION)? It is documented, but it means 199 of 200 conform.

findings.detail: The docstring says a test cross-checks step_names() against replayer_steps(). replayer_steps() (line 95) is called nowhere in the repository; I grepped for it. tests/test_h19_conformance.py::test_step_names_match_the_proof_files only asserts that step_names() contains a hard-coded set of names. EXPERIMENTS.md line 43 repeats the claim. A guard that names a step the proofs lack is therefore not caught.

Replay cannot fail on the endpoint heartbeat refusal. govsim/trace.py line 182 emits heartbeat_lost for the governor just before every execute_refused with reason ENDPOINT_HEARTBEAT_EXPIRED. So m.heartbeat is always False when the 'refused for an expired heartbeat, but heartbeat is live' check runs. This is the same circularity the revision claimed to remove. EXPERIMENTS.md line 41 says the guards 'can fail on it'; that is shown only for the governor-side expiry (halt.cause), not for the endpoint-side expiry. No test makes the check fail.

The brief asks for a replayer that drives the abstract machine of core_invariants.py and commit_point.py. Replay instead executes a hand-copied concrete re-encoding. Its guards are compared with the Z3 steps neither symbolically nor by a test. The docstring (lines 8-14) admits this. Taken together with the finding at line 11, the link between theorem and simulation is not mechanical. Please report this as a deviation, not as completion.

The stale-edition fixture asserts only that 'execute_ok' is in the message. Every NoTransition message contains the event string, so any refusal at an execute_ok passes. Line 100 for the halted-issue fixture is stronger ('halted'), but it too does not pin the step. The fixtures also bypass the check by monkeypatching (state set to RUN, commit_from_endpoint stubbed, ep.epoch overwritten) rather than commenting out one check. Assert the step name and reason.

'199 clean plus that one expected refusal' is not backed by a committed artifact or an exact-count assertion. The acceptance test asserts only len(results) >= 200 (tests/test_h19_conformance.py line 40). H19_REPORT is not committed. The glob test_h*.py counts every test in those files, and tests that drive no governor pass vacuously (the test file admits this at line 49). The acceptance wording 'all 200 tests' is therefore not shown.

'the machine is looser than the system there, which is sound' (stutters for expiry, wrong endpoint, parameter mismatch, bad signature) is asserted. No test shows these refusals are stutters in the sense of the proof. Whether endpoints.py really burns before commit and device checks (line 36) was not checked against endpoints.py. It is supported only by the single test at tests/test_h19_conformance.py line 137.

FAULT_INJECTION exempts an existing test by name and turns its teardown into an expected failure. The reason is documented and asserted, so this is not gaming, but the brief says all traces replay. The disproof outcome ('a step the machine does not have') should be filed in EXPERIMENTS.md as such, which was done at line 38. Also, tests/h19_plugin.py is a new, unlisted file; check that the brief allows it.

hold_released is inserted into the event list ahead of its ticket_issued and every seq is renumbered, so the trace is not the order things happened. This is documented (lines 40-44). The reordering decides whether the commit-point check passes, so the 'a ticket without clearance fails' result rests on the sink's heuristic: it matches the last ticket for the same action hash. If no ticket is found, the release is appended.
'assert "arm" not in rep.steps' is vacuous, because arms are counted in Report.arms and never via report.count('arm'). The test shows only that arms >= 1.

claims.claim: All traces of the H0 to H18 tests replay clean except one injected fault: 199 clean plus 1 expected refusal
claims.evidence: tests/test_h19_conformance.py asserts len(results) >= 200 and faulted == FAULT_INJECTION. There is no exact count and no committed artifact. The suite total of 207 less the 7 acceptance tests gives 200.

claims.claim: Two broken-governor fixtures (halted governor signs, stale-edition ticket executes) fail replay with the event named
claims.evidence: Both tests exist and pass. They name only the event kind, and both bypass the checks by monkeypatching.

claims.claim: A test cross-checks the step names the replayer drives against the proof files
claims.evidence: replayer_steps() is defined but never called. The test only checks that step_names() contains a literal set.

claims.claim: The heartbeat is a first-class event, so the issue and execute guards read state the events set and can fail on it
claims.evidence: The governor-side halt.cause path is real. The endpoint-expiry path emits heartbeat_lost immediately before the guard that reads it, so the CLAIM_HB check at proofs/replay.py line 317 cannot fail.

claims.claim: Gap in the theorem: a power cycle is not a step; govsim boots HALTED_INITIAL and reaches RUN with no clear
claims.evidence: core_invariants.py has no boot step, and 'halted' is free in the init state. The replayer counts arms, and test_the_first_run_after_a_boot... shows arms >= 1. I did not read govsim/governor.py.

claims.claim: Gap in the theorem: the endpoint burns a ticket before commit and device checks and may then refuse (burn without execute)
claims.evidence: A fixture burns a ticket via a halted committer and asserts consumed and not executed. I did not read endpoints.py.

claims.claim: Refusals for expiry, wrong endpoint, parameter mismatch and bad signature are stutters of forged execute; the machine is looser, which is sound
claims.evidence: The code treats them as stutters (ADMIT_REFUSALS). No test or proof shows soundness.

claims.claim: The guards are a concrete re-encoding of the Z3 steps; the guard logic is not compared symbolically
claims.evidence: This is an honest caveat, consistent with proofs/replay.py. The guards do match the issue/execute/forged_execute guards in core_invariants.py lines 87-104 when read by eye.

claims.claim: P1 to P4 re-checked after each step is a consistency guard, not independent evidence
claims.evidence: check_invariants in proofs/replay.py. The claim is self-limiting and accurate.

claims.claim: Acceptance: pytest -q tests/test_h19_conformance.py passes against all 200 tests' traces
claims.evidence: verify.json: exit 0. The replay runs in a subprocess with a >= 200 threshold. The summary is empty, so this is the brief's claim, not the agent's.
